tldr: Kimi K2 is a 1.04 trillion-parameter MoE LLM with 32B activated parameters that achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source non-thinking models, particularly in agentic and software engineering tasks, enabled by the novel MuonClip optimizer and a large-scale agentic data synthesis pipeline.
contributions: MuonClip optimizer combining Muon with QK-Clip for stable training without loss spikes
Large-scale agentic data synthesis pipeline generating tool-use demonstrations via simulated and real-world environments
General RL framework combining verifiable rewards (RLVR) with self-critique rubric reward mechanism
Open-sourcing of base and post-trained model checkpoints for agentic intelligence research
methods: Kimi K2 is a 1.04T-parameter MoE transformer (32B activated) pre-trained on 15.5T high-quality tokens using the novel MuonClip optimizer, which integrates Muon with a per-head weight-clipping mechanism (QK-Clip) to control exploding attention logits. Pre-training also employs synthetic data rephrasing for Knowledge and Mathematics domains to improve token utility. Post-training includes a multi-stage process featuring a large-scale agentic data synthesis pipeline and joint reinforcement learning combining verifiable rewards with self-critique rubric rewards.
results: K2 achieves 66.1 on Tau2-Bench, 76.5 on ACEBench (En), 65.8 on SWE-Bench Verified, and 47.3 on SWE-Bench Multilingual, surpassing most open and closed baselines in non-thinking settings. It scores 53.7 on LiveCodeBench v6, 49.5 on AIME 2025, 75.1 on GPQA-Diamond, and 27.1 on OJBench. Training on 15.5T tokens completed with zero loss spikes. K2 ranks as the top open-source model on LMSYS Arena (July 17, 2025). Sparsity scaling experiments show sparsity 48 reduces FLOPs by 1.69× compared to sparsity 8 for equivalent validation loss.
limitations: Synthetic data rephrasing faces challenges in generalizing across diverse source domains without compromising factual accuracy, minimizing hallucinations and unintended toxicity, and ensuring scalability to large-scale datasets. Multi-epoch repetition of training data yields diminishing returns and increases overfitting risk. Increasing sparsity improves performance but comes with increased infrastructure complexity.
